identity.name: Thonburi Kingdom
native_names: อาณาจักรธนบุรี
กรุงธนบุรี

land.text: Ayutthaya and the Chao Phraya basin, which Taksin retook from the Burmese in November 1767

predecessors.note: Ayutthaya fell on 7 April 1767; 'Phraya Tak reconquered Ayutthaya-Thonburi area in November 1767' (Burmese-Siamese War 1765-1767 page). Cliopatria's Ayutthaya row runs to 1768 and Thonburi starts in 1769.

land.text: the whole Thonburi shape, held by Chakri as Rama I from April 1782

successors.note: Infobox successor Rattanakosin Kingdom: 'April 1782: Chakri became King Rama I, founding the Rattanakosin Kingdom' after Taksin was deposed on 1 April 1782.

capitals.name: Thonburi (Bangkok)
capitals.note: Infobox capital Thonburi; Taksin 'enthroned himself at Thonburi in December 1767' (infobox: 28 December 1767). The page does not say when Rama I moved to Bangkok across the river in 1782.

rulers.name: Taksin (Phraya Tak, King Taksin the Great)
rulers.note: Enthroned 28 December 1767; deposed 1 April 1782 (infobox). The infobox's 'Inthraphithak' entry is garbled.

correction.text: the Ayutthaya-Thonburi area on the Chao Phraya plus the eastern coast from Chonburi to Chanthaburi

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1767-1768: the state begins at Taksin's coronation in December 1767 with the Chao Phraya heartland and the eastern coast (Chonburi and Rayong taken in January 1767 and Chanthaburi in June 1767, infobox and text), not with the 360,000 km2 Cliopatria draws from 1769. Rival regimes held Phimai, Phitsanulok, Nakhon Si Thammarat and Fang (Phimai fell in 1768).

union.text: Lan Na south of Chiang Mai (Lamphun, Lampang) and Nan, outside Thonburi until January 1775

minus.text: the 1769 shape without Phitsanulok (the rival regime of Fang) and without Lan Na and Nan
Pattani, Yala and Narathiwat, the Malay sultanates that 'sent tributes to Thonburi in 1769' and ignored Taksin's request of 1776

correction.text: the 1769 shape without Phitsanulok (the rival regime of Fang), without Lan Na and Nan, and without the Malay north (Pattani, Yala, Narathiwat), which is tributary and not direct land

keyframe_review.note: 1769 (360,015 km2): the shape holds Siam from Phitsanulok to Songkhla and the Malay north, with Nan, Lamphun and Lampang. In 1769 Phitsanulok was still in the hands of the rival Fang ('Taksin retook it in August 1770'), and Lan Na and Nan only 'came under Thonburi control' in 1775 (Burmese-held Chiang Mai fell in January 1775). Nakhon Si Thammarat fell on 21 September 1769 (infobox; 'October 1769' in the text), so it belongs from this year. The correction is for 1769 only; 1770-1774 follows in the next keyframe. [Repaired 2026-10-19 after review: Pattani, Yala and Narathiwat (100, 100 and 93 per cent of the shape) removed: the page has the sultanates 'sent tributes to Thonburi in 1769' and the ledger records a tributary relation, 1769-1776 (vassal tint), so they are not direct land. Rattanakosin's 1782 shape is likewise drawn without them.]

minus.text: Lan Na south of Chiang Mai (Lamphun, Lampang) and Nan, outside Thonburi until January 1775
the 1769 shape with Phitsanulok, without Lan Na and Nan
Pattani, Yala and Narathiwat, the Malay sultanates that 'sent tributes to Thonburi in 1769' and ignored Taksin's request of 1776

correction.text: the 1769 shape with Phitsanulok, without Lan Na, Nan and the Malay north (Pattani, Yala, Narathiwat)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1770-1774: Phitsanulok is retaken (infobox 8 August 1770; 'Fang escaped and vanished'), 'Taksin's position was secured after the last rival fell'; Lan Na and Nan are not yet Siamese. The Malay north (Pattani, Yala, Narathiwat, Songkhla) is drawn as direct land in the Cliopatria shape although Pattani, Terengganu and perhaps Kedah only 'sent tribute' in 1769 and ignored Taksin's requests in 1776; the ledger records the tributary status. [Repaired 2026-10-19 after review: the Malay north the note above calls tributary is now taken out of the shape, as the ledger says (vassal_start 1769, vassal_end 1776).]

1775-1780: Lan Na and Nan are inside: 'Lanna came under Thonburi control' and 'Nan also came under its power that year' (Thonburi page); 'appointed Phaya Chaban as governor of Chiang Mai and Kawila as governor of Lampang in 1775' (Chiang Mai page). Chiang Mai itself (Cliopatria's Chiangmai row, 52,000 km2) is a tributary and is not in this shape. Laos (Champasak 1778, Vientiane 1779) is dependency land, not in the shape. Infobox area: none ('a 1780 sphere-of-influence map'). [Repaired 2026-10-19 after review: verdict ok -> adjust. Nan is a vassal in the ledger (vassal_start 1775, 'The princedom of Nan also came under the power of Thonburi in 1775') and is removed from the direct-land shape so that it keeps the vassal tint; Pattani, Yala and Narathiwat are removed as in 1769 (tributary only; Rattanakosin founds in 1782 without them). Lampang and Lamphun stay in the shape: a gain from the Konbaung is now in the ledger (January 1775, 'Thonburi took control of Lanna in 1775').]

Taksin was deposed on 1 April 1782 (infobox) and the shape passes whole to the Rattanakosin Kingdom. [Repaired 2026-10-19 after review: verdict ok -> adjust, same two removals as the 1775 keyframe (Nan tinted, Pattani, Yala and Narathiwat tributary and out of the shape until Rattanakosin's gain of 1786).]

region.text: the Ayutthaya-Thonburi area and the eastern coast

ledger.note: 28 December 1767: Taksin is crowned at Thonburi. Ayutthaya fell in April 1767; he took Chanthaburi in June 1767; Phraya Tak 'reconquered Ayutthaya-Thonburi area in November 1767' and was 'newly enthroned as King Taksin in December 1767' and moved the royal seat to Thonburi (Burmese-Siamese War 1765-1767 page). Infobox 'Existence: 1767-1782'.

region.text: Phimai and the Khorat plateau around it

ledger.note: 1768: Thonburi conquers Phimai. 'Phimai, 1768: Thonburi conquered it that year' (the rival regime of Phimai in the Khorat country).

region.text: the Malay north: Pattani, Yala and Narathiwat

ledger.note: 1769: Pattani sends tribute. 'Pattani, Terengganu, and possibly Kedah sent tribute' in 1769; in 1776 Taksin 'asked Pattani, Kelantan, and Terengganu for military and monetary support, but they ignored him' and in 1786 'Siam resumed real control over the northern sultanates'.

region.text: Cambodia and the Ha Tien coast

ledger.note: 1769: Taksin presses Cambodia for tribute and invades 'that year without success'; the real invasion comes in 1771.

region.text: Nakhon Si Thammarat (Ligor) and the south it ruled

ledger.note: 21 September 1769: Taksin captures Nakhon Si Thammarat. The text gives October 1769, the infobox 21 September 1769. The southern rival regime falls and the south is Siamese again.

region.text: Taksin retakes Phitsanulok

ledger.note: 8 August 1770: Taksin retakes Phitsanulok. 'Taksin retook it in August 1770 (infobox: 8 August 1770). Fang escaped and vanished.' The last rival falls and 'Taksin's position was secured'.

region.text: Hà Tiên and the Cambodian coast

ledger.note: November 1771: the Siamese take Hà Tiên. 'He invaded Cambodia and Hà Tiên, which fell in November 1771'; he returned to Thonburi in December 1771 after installing Ang Non. In July 1772 Vietnamese forces 'seize control of Phnom Penh and Cambodia'.

region.text: Hà Tiên and the Cambodian coast

ledger.note: 1773: the Siamese leave Cambodia and Hà Tiên. 'Siamese troops withdrew from Cambodia and Hà Tiên, after about 10,000 Cambodians were taken to Siam.'

region.text: Cambodia and the Ha Tien coast

ledger.note: 1773: the Siamese leave Cambodia; Ang Ton abdicated in favour of Ang Non in 1775 and Ang Non was murdered in 1779 (Thonburi page).

region.text: Nan comes under Thonburi's power ('Nan also came under its power that year')

ledger.note: 1775: Nan comes under Thonburi's power ('Nan also came under its power that year'). Nan is a principality without a Cliopatria row; the admin-1 unit stands for it. [Repair 2026-10-19: Nan is now removed from the 1775 and 1781 keyframes, so it is drawn only as this vassal tint.]

region.text: the Lampang and Lamphun cells of the Thonburi shape, the Lan Na land south of Chiang Mai that Cliopatria gives to Thonburi (the rest of both provinces is in the Chiangmai row)

ledger.note: January 1775: Thonburi takes Lampang and Lamphun from the Burmese. 'Thonburi took control of Lanna in 1775, ending the 200 years of Burmese vassalage'; Chaophraya Chakri led the vanguard to Lampang, and Kawila of Lampang had risen against the Burmese; 'Chiang Mai fell in January 1775' (Thonburi page, reopened). Taksin appointed Phaya Chaban and Kawila governors of Chiang Mai and Lampang in 1775 (the Chiang Mai page calls them 'vassal rulers'). The year is the page's; the page does not name Lamphun or give its governor, and the split of the two provinces between this state's shape (58 and 77 per cent) and the Chiangmai row (42 and 23 per cent) is an artefact of Cliopatria's two rows, so the region is my reading of the shape (confidence 2). The konbaung-dynasty ledger now records the matching loss. [Added 2026-10-19 after review.]

region.text: Chiang Mai and the north (Lan Na)

ledger.note: 15 January 1775: Chiang Mai is taken from the Burmese and made a Siamese tributary. 'Taksin of Thonburi marched his army north to attack Burmese-held Chiang Mai' in December 1774; 'Siamese conquest 15 January 1775' (infobox); Phaya Chaban was appointed governor of Chiang Mai and Kawila of Lampang (Chiang Mai page); 'Lanna came under Thonburi tributary'.

region.text: Sawankhalok, Sukhothai and Phitsanulok

ledger.note: October 1775: the Burmese invade northern Siam. Satpagyon Bo came through the Three Pagodas Pass in February 1775 and surrendered at Bangkaeo in March 1775; 'Maha Thiha Thura marched his massive army of 35,000 men ... into Northern Siam in October 1775' and took Sawankhalok and Sukhothai.

region.text: the Malay north

ledger.note: 1776: the Malay north stops obeying. Taksin 'asked Pattani, Kelantan, and Terengganu for military and monetary support, but they ignored him' (1776). Page silent on a formal end; Siam 'resumed real control over the northern sultanates' only in 1786 (Rattanakosin).

region.text: Sawankhalok, Sukhothai and Phitsanulok

ledger.note: August 1776: the Burmese leave Siam. Phitsanulok fell on 15 March 1776 and was 'utterly and completely destroyed'; 'The Burmese had left Siam by August 1776' and Hsinbyushin died on 10 June 1776.

region.text: the kingdom of Luang Prabang

ledger.note: 1778: Luang Prabang is a Siamese vassal. The Kingdom of Luang Phrabang page: 'Vassal of Siam (1778-1893)'. The Thonburi page has Taksin launch 'the invasion of Laos' in 1778, after which Surasi captured Champasak.

region.text: the kingdom of Champasak

ledger.note: 1778: Surasi captures Champasak. 'Surasi captured Champasak, and the Emerald Buddha and Phra Bang images were taken in 1778.' The champasak dossier has the occupation 1778-1779.

region.text: the kingdom of Champasak

ledger.note: 1779: the occupation of Champasak ends. Page silent: the Thonburi page gives only the capture in 1778; the champasak dossier cites a page for the withdrawal in 1779.

region.text: the kingdom of Vientiane

ledger.note: March 1779: Vientiane falls and becomes a Siamese dependency. 'In 1779, Siamese forces sacked Vientiane ... King Ong Boun decided to submit to the Siamese and Vientiane became a Siamese dependency' (Vientiane page, 'Siamese vassal from 1779'); the Thonburi infobox gives March 1779.

region.text: the Thonburi shape

ledger.note: 1 April 1782: Taksin is deposed and Chakri becomes Rama I. 'April 1782: Chakri became King Rama I, founding the Rattanakosin Kingdom'; 'Taksin was deposed (infobox 1 April 1782)'. The tributaries pass to the new dynasty.

wars.name: Taksin's reconquest of Siam
wars.outcome: Taksin took Chanthaburi (June 1767), Ayutthaya-Thonburi (November 1767), Phimai (1768), Nakhon Si Thammarat (21 September 1769) and Phitsanulok (8 August 1770); 'Taksin's position was secured after the last rival fell'.
wars.note: The page dates none of the rival regimes' foundations; the Burmese war page has Taksin reconquering the Chao Phraya region in November 1767.

wars.name: Siamese invasions of Cambodia and Hà Tiên
wars.outcome: A failed invasion in 1769; Hà Tiên fell in November 1771 and Ang Non was installed in Cambodia; Vietnamese forces took Phnom Penh in July 1772 and the Siamese withdrew in 1773.

wars.name: Thonburi's Burmese wars (1771-1776)
wars.outcome: Burmese raids on Sawankhalok (1771) and Phichai (1772-1773), the Burmese defeat at Bangkaeo (March 1775) and the Siamese capture of Chiang Mai (15 January 1775); the Burmese took Sukhothai and Phitsanulok in 1775-1776 and left by August 1776.
wars.note: Infobox of the war page: October 1775 - August 1776, 'Siamese victory; depopulation of Northern Cities and destruction of Phitsanulok'.

wars.name: Siamese conquest of Lan Na (1774-1775)
wars.outcome: Chiang Mai was taken on 15 January 1775 with the help of Kawila of Lampang; Lan Na became a Thonburi tributary under Phaya Chaban; Chiang Mai was abandoned after a Burmese attack in 1777.

wars.name: Siamese conquest of Laos (1777-1779)
wars.outcome: Surasi captured Champasak in 1778; Vientiane fell in March 1779 and became a Siamese dependency; Luang Prabang is a Siamese vassal from 1778 (its own page).
wars.note: Thonburi page: 'the governor of Nangrong rebelled with Champasak's support' in 1777; about ten thousand Lao were deported in 1779.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line: Siam's frontiers with Burma, the Malay sultanates, Cambodia and the Lao kingdoms are approximate and the tributaries are tints.

notes:
Page budget 1-2; the Thonburi page is the base, and five pages opened for the Burmese, Chiang Mai and Lao dossiers of this batch supply the rest (WebFetch summaries, so every quotation is the summariser's quotation). The Thonburi infobox gives no area; Cliopatria's shape is 360,000 km2 (Central Siam, the Malay north to Narathiwat, the Khorat country to Buri Ram, and the north to Nan, Phrae and Tak).

Cliopatria's three shapes (1769-1774, 1775-1780, 1781-1782) are one outline. Corrections: the state begins in December 1767, not 1769, with the Chao Phraya heartland and the eastern coast; the shape from 1769 contains Phitsanulok (retaken only in August 1770) and Lamphun, Lampang and Nan (only 'under Thonburi's power' from 1775); the Malay north is tributary land, not direct.

Tributaries (recorded here as vassal_start): Pattani (1769 and ignored from 1776), Chiang Mai (15 January 1775), Nan (1775), Luang Prabang (1778), Vientiane (March 1779); no matching ends because they continue under the Rattanakosin Kingdom. Champasak is an occupation in the champasak dossier (1778-1779); I record the capture of 1778 only and close it at confidence 1.

Counterparts needing dossiers: phimai (a rival regime in the Khorat country, to 1768), nakhon-si-thammarat (the southern rival regime, to September 1769), chao-phra-fang (Fang, at Phitsanulok, to August 1770), nan (principality; 1775), patani-kingdom (Cliopatria row 1572-1690 only; the sultanate lasted to 1902).

Repair after review (2026-10-19). (1) Pattani, Yala and Narathiwat are taken out of the 1769, 1770, 1775 and 1781 keyframes: the page has them only as tributaries ('sent tributes to Thonburi in 1769'; 'the degree of actual Siamese control over the Malay sultanates in the Thonburi Period was doubtful'; they ignored the 1776 request), the ledger has the vassal tint 1769-1776, and the Rattanakosin dossier founds in 1782 without them and gains them in 1786, so the Malay north no longer flickers into Siam at the 1782 seam. The page does not mention Songkhla, which stays in the shape. (2) Nan is taken out of the 1775 and 1781 keyframes (princedom, vassal tint). (3) New gain of January 1775: the Lampang and Lamphun cells of the shape, from the Konbaung (the konbaung-dynasty dossier splits its 1775 loss between chiangmai and thonburi-kingdom). I disagree in one respect with the reviewer: the Chiang Mai page calls Kawila of Lampang a 'vassal ruler', so Lampang may belong with the Chiangmai tributary rather than with direct Thonburi land; I followed the review because Cliopatria draws 58 per cent of Lampang and 77 per cent of Lamphun as Thonburi land and the other row draws the rest.
